content:
Smithland Lock and Dam is located on the Ohio River in Livingston County, Kentucky. It was completed in 1929 by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers as a part of the Ohio River navigation system. The lock and dam system plays a crucial role in maintaining water levels for navigation and controlling flooding along the river.

The lock at Smithland Lock and Dam measures 110 feet wide by 600 feet long and can handle barges up to 1,200 feet in length. It is utilized by commercial traffic as well as recreational boaters navigating the Ohio River.

In addition to its navigation functions, Smithland Lock and Dam also serves as a barrier to prevent invasive species from moving upstream, such as Asian carp, which can disrupt the ecosystem of the river.

Overall, Smithland Lock and Dam is an essential piece of infrastructure that helps to facilitate commerce and transportation on the Ohio River while also providing flood control and environmental protection measures.
